```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
source("harness/long_drought.R")   # loads plant; rainfall records and mkenv()
source("harness/schedule/refine.R")
p <- scm_base_parameters("TF24")
p <- add_strategies(p, trait_matrix(0.32, "lma"))
```

# The whole thing

The quantities a run reports are J, a strategy's fitness (its offspring per seed over a
patch's life), and J's elasticity with respect to each trait. Each has a tolerance ε, set
once per quantity: a tenth of its spread across eight rainfall records, never under 0.01.
Curvatures and invaders' quantities are not yet judged (see the end).

Every one of them is a sum over birth date, so a node schedule is a rule for that sum.
The schedule has two parts:

- **Breakpoints:** births where a recruit's fate is not smooth in birth date. These are
  the ends of each establishment spell, and on some records the birth date after which
  cohorts stall under the canopy. A first, cheap run's establishment record gives the
  spell ends.
- **A density and a level.** Each spell holds an even number of intervals, its nodes at
  equal shares of a density that says where fate curves most. Level k doubles every count
  k times, so each level's nodes contain every node of the level below.

A run estimates its own error. Replay it on its own steps with every other node inside
each spell removed. A third of the change estimates the run's error, in every quantity at
once. The run reports its value corrected by that estimate. If any quantity's bound is over
its limit, go up a level or more and run again; the rejected run is then the new run's
estimate, with no replay. The schedule is kept: the other runs of an analysis around the
same traits use it unchanged, and each reports its own estimate.

```{r whole, eval = FALSE}
fit <- refine_schedule(p, mkenv("episodic"), ctrl)  # ctrl as in harness/schedule/refine_case.R
fit$answer     # ln J and its elasticities: the last run corrected by its estimate
fit$estimate   # each quantity's estimated error, in units of its ε
fit$bound      # what the stop compares with 1
fit$schedule   # breakpoints, density, counts; nodes_of(fit$schedule, fit$level)
fit$history    # each pass: its level, answer, estimate, worst bound
fit$status     # converged, unconverged or failed
```

# What a node is

On the birth-date coordinate a node is the cohort born at one instant. The individuals
born between two neighbouring nodes form an interval, and the interval carries two
things:

- **Its count.** The run integrates the establishment rate exactly over the interval,
  together with its first moment.
- **Its members' fate.** Their survival, size and seed output are taken to vary linearly
  in birth date between the two nodes.

Every stand total has the same form: J, the leaf area above a height, the water drawn
from a soil layer. Each is a sum over intervals of count × interpolated fate.

The schedule's error is the error of that sum:

- **Where fate is smooth across an interval,** the error is about
  count × width² × fate's curvature, so it falls four-fold when the spacing halves.
- **The error adds over birth date.** Errors measured region by region add to the whole
  run's within 0.04ε.
- **A local error reaches every cohort.** An interval that over-counts leaf area or
  uptake changes the light and water every other cohort meets.

# Breakpoints

**Net production decides everything.** An individual's net production is

    P = a_bio · a_y · (A − R) − T

where A is the leaf's optimal assimilation, set by the light at its crown and the water
its roots reach. P drives each process:

- **P > 0:** the individual grows and fills its storage pool.
- **P < 0:** the pool drains, and the hazard a_dG1 · exp(−a_dG2 · r) rises as relative
  storage r falls.
- **Establishment:** a newborn establishes only if its P at seed height is positive.

A seedling's roots lie in the top 0.3 m of soil, so establishment follows the top
layer's water. A rain starts an establishment spell within a day, and the stand's uptake
dries the layer until the spell ends. Between spells nothing establishes.

**At a spell's opening, fate's slope jumps.**
- A cohort born just before an opening waits for rain, so a later birth waits less and
  does better.
- After the opening, each later cohort meets more shade, so it does worse.
- On dry, fate's slope was +0.5e-3 per day before every one of 22 openings and
  −2.2e-3 per day after.

**At a spell's end, the count stops.**
- Fate itself is continuous there. Within the spell its curvature rises 1.3–5× toward
  the end, and the cohorts' sensitivity to the hydraulic traits curves up to 17× harder.
- An interval that reaches past the end into the gap takes its members' fate from the gap's different curve.
  Its error is then set by how far its last node sits from the end, not by the spacing.

So both ends of every spell are breakpoints. With them, the worst errors on dry,
long-wet and episodic with lma ×1.25 fell from 1.1–3.4ε to 0.47–0.79ε.

**A spell's end moves with the schedule.** The end is where the stand's uptake dries the
top layer, and that uptake depends on the nodes. Ends moved by a median of 0.48 days
between schedules, and the first spell's end by 12 days; openings did not move. Even so, the
loop takes spell ends once, from its first run, and keeps them. Re-reading them each pass
would break the nesting of levels, and then every pass would need its own replay. Using one
pilot's ends throughout, the graded layout passed on all five cases.

**On constant rain there is one more breakpoint.**
- Cohorts born in the first 23.5 days reach the canopy.
- Every later cohort stalls under them: its P falls below zero and comes back.
- Survival to the end of the run falls from 0.63 to 0.02 across 0.03 days of birth date.

In the model's equations, fate stops being smooth only where a cohort's sequence of P
sign changes differs from its neighbour's (`docs/dynamics.md`).
- With a diagnostic build that counts each node's sign changes, the count goes from 0 to
  2 exactly at the stall.
- Bisecting the pair of nodes whose counts differ placed the stall to 0.0003 day in five
  rounds.
- Today's runs do not record that count, so the loop does not place a stall boundary yet.

**Finding spell ends.** A forward run on about 100 even introductions places 98–100% of
openings within a day of the finest run's, and 75–89% of ends. It costs 0.09–0.13 of a
full run.

**Invaders establish on their own net production,** so their spells can end on other days
than the resident's. An invader is introduced only at the resident's birth dates, so the
breakpoints should include the invaders' spell ends as well. That is not built, and no run
has tested it.

# The density and the level

A breakpoint is never removed. Between breakpoints, each spell gets an even number of
intervals, set by its share of the density and the level, and its nodes sit at equal shares
of the density. Level 0 is at scale 1: a spell's count is its share of the density, at
the spacings below. A spell whose share holds at most one interval keeps one; otherwise its count
is rounded up to even and given two more. Four shapes in fate set the density:

- **The first cohorts.** Births before the first spell ends produce 70–97% of J. Their
  fate falls nearly exponentially in birth date, with a decay length of 0.4–1.2 years,
  because a later birth reproduces later, against the patch's disturbance and the stand's
  drought mortality.
- **The understory.**
  - Within a spell, a later birth is a smaller copy that has had less time to die, so its
    leaf area is convex in birth date.
  - Straight lines between nodes over-count that leaf area by 0.5–1.1% (3–4% in the
    first years). Through the light or the water the stand creates (the measurements
    disagree on which), the first cohorts carry most of that error as extra drought
    mortality.
- **The last three weeks of a spell.** A seedling born there starts the coming drought
  with fuller reserves, and every one of them empties its reserves. The cohorts'
  sensitivity to the hydraulic and storage traits curves 3–17× harder than a month
  earlier. The rise spans about t_r = o·ln(a_st3·a_dG2), the time a seedling's reserves
  take to run down: 19.4 days at these traits, within 26% of the measured width on every
  case, and twice as wide when the storage offset doubles. The density rises to about 2×
  over that width, and each spell gets two more intervals for it.
- **Late births.** They produce little J but still draw down the water. Late intervals
  wider than about 160 days leave the square law on the traits that act through the soil.

The density comes from the first run's offspring per node, and its ages from T(t), the
share of J still to be produced after calendar time t (as built, `spacing_of()`):
- **before the first spell ends,** the spacing is a 24th of that time while the first
  cohorts' offspring are within tenfold of the first cohort's, and a 12th after;
- **later,** it is 90 days where offspring are at the spells' median, and wider where they
  are far below it, capped at 100 days until t50 (half of J produced) and 280 days after;
- **after t90** (90% produced), spell edges are no longer breakpoints: everything later is
  one stretch.
- **before each spell end,** the density is doubled within 0.95 t_r of the end, tapering
  to no change by 1.4 t_r.

On the ten-case bank t50 and t90 land at about 16–24 and 23–29 years, where fixed ages had
put them. In a shorter run they move earlier with it.

The late caps are wider than the 45–80 days where elasticities were measured on the square
law. The five cases passed regardless, because late births carry little of J; it is listed
as open below.

**A spell too short to hold two intervals** keeps one, and the replay does not see it.
Such spells hold much of the establishment but 0.5–6.6% of J; on five cases their error
was at most 0.22ε, and that maximum is added to every bound.

# How a run estimates its own error

Remove every other node inside each spell, and replay the run on its own steps:

    estimated error ≈ (Q with every other node removed − Q) / 3

Why it can be trusted:

- **Every interval is merged once.** Each spell holds an even number of intervals, so
  the removal merges them all in pairs. With an odd count, one interval per spell is
  never merged; in the first tests that hid 17 of 70 spell ends, and 39 more sat in
  spells with no node inside to remove.
- **Each removed node sits at the middle of what it merges, by share of the density.**
  The factor 1/3 is exact for a node at the middle in width. Off the middle it is
  (l³ + (1 − l)³)/(3 l (1 − l)) for a node at fraction l. With the graded density the
  replay estimated the error at 0.97 of its size in one run on dry.
- **The replay shares the run's steps,** so step-size choices add nothing to the
  difference.
- **The replay includes the stand's response.** A removed node changes the light and
  water every cohort meets, and the replay recomputes that.
- **Measured:** with both spell ends as breakpoints and the grading before them, the
  estimate was 0.82–1.17 of the error on dry, long-wet, episodic with lma ×1.25, dry-flat
  and episodic with a_dG2 ×0.8 (cosine 0.95–1.00 once short spells are set aside). The
  worst errors were 0.30–0.56ε, at or under those of T0, the tuned schedule the loop
  replaces, on every case.
- **Cost:** 0.51–0.66 of a run.

**Report the corrected answer.** Since the estimate reads most of the error, the run reports
Q − e, not Q. The correction costs nothing, being the same runs. On the five cases the worst
true error fell from 0.20–0.61ε (Q) to 0.03–0.20ε (Q − e).

**The bound** on the corrected answer is

    0.5 |e| + u

and the loop stops when every quantity's bound is under its ε.
- **The coefficient 0.5 is empirical.** It holds while the estimate reads at least two
  thirds of the error. Over the cases tested, the bound covered 375 of 376
  quantity-cases.
- **u covers what the estimate cannot see.** After a replay, that is the spells too short
  to hold two intervals: at most 0.22ε. After a doubled pass (below), it is the change of
  steps between the pair's two runs: 0.08ε.
- **The ODE tolerance's own error is not in the bound.** The replay shares the run's steps,
  so it cannot see that error, and no node schedule can fix it. The step controller holds it
  instead (`design-grid-controller.md`). At 1e-4 it reached 0.61ε in one quantity on dry
  with lma ×1.25.

**Scale 1 is canonical.** On the five cases at scale 1 the first pass was accepted every
time. Started at half scale, every first pass was rejected
(1.0–1.8) and every second pass accepted, with the worst error 0.26–0.66ε. The bound covered
every quantity but one: on episodic with a_dG2 ×0.8, a_l1 erred 0.66ε against a bound of
0.55. Its first level was short of the square law, so its estimate read low.

**Where the error is.** The run's own reverse sweep, with a small addition, also gives
J's error by stretch of birth date, to 0.03ε, for 7.5% more than the run. This node-drop map
is measured but not yet part of the loop.

# The loop

```
  first run (100 even introductions, forward only)
        │ establishment spells, offspring curve, T(t)
        ▼
  breakpoints (spell edges up to t90), density, level 0 at scale 1
        │
        ▼
  run level 0 ──► replay with every other node in each spell removed
        │         e = (Q_removed − Q) / 3,  u = 0.22ε
        ▼
  every quantity's bound 0.5|e| + u under ε?
        │ yes: report Q − e; keep the schedule for the analysis
        │ no:  go up j levels, the fewest whose predicted bound
        │      0.5|e| / 4^j + 0.08 is under 0.9ε (never above level 4),
        │      and run it. The rejected run is its estimate:
        │      e = (Q_coarse − Q_fine) / (4^j − 1),  u = 0.08ε.  Check again.
        │      After four passes, or at level 4: report the finest run as
        │      unconverged. A failed run or a non-finite quantity ends the loop
        │      with the last complete pass, flagged as failed.
```

- **Every full run is a candidate answer;** no run is made only to be compared with.
- **It stops.** Each rejected pass at least doubles every count, which cuts the error at
  least fourfold on the square law, and the caps report a failure instead of running on.
- **Doubling, not rescaling.** Doubling keeps the levels nested, so the rejected run is
  the next run's estimate and needs no replay. A rescale by √(bound/ε) would not nest, and
  would need its own replay. Starting at half scale and doubling cost 1.56–1.74× a scale-1
  run plus its replay, which is why scale 1 is the start.
- **The kept schedule serves an analysis.** Each later run on it can report its own
  estimate. One over its limit, or a large move in the traits, refines a new schedule.
  Reporting each run's distance from the traits the schedule was refined at is not built.

# What it adapts to

| what varies | why | what responds |
|---|---|---|
| when spells start and end | the rainfall record and the stand's uptake | breakpoints, from the first run's establishment record |
| where fate curves | first cohorts, understory, a spell's last weeks, late births | the density and the level |
| how large the error is | about 100× across trait × climate | the replay estimates it on each run |
| which quantities bind | different traits on different cases | every quantity has its own ε |
| how a local error spreads | light and water reach every cohort | the replay recomputes the stand's response |
| simulation length | when J is produced | the density's ages, from T(t) |
| how fast reserves run down | the storage traits | the width of the grading before spell ends, t_r |

Not yet built: a stall boundary on constant rain, placed by bisection; invaders' spell
ends among the breakpoints.

# Traits

The traits move the breakpoints by moving where P = 0:
- Carbon gain, carbon cost and water access set the light and water at which P
  vanishes, and so when spells start and end.
- Height growth sets who ends up shaded.
- The storage pool sets how costly a time below zero is.

On constant rain:
- lma ×0.8 and ×1.25 move the stall from day 23.6 to 27.1 and 18.9;
- hmat ×0.8 and ×1.25 move it to days 45–50 and 9.9–10.9.

A schedule refined at one set of traits serves nearby ones, but the error grows as the
traits move. A run at moved traits on the kept schedule costs that run plus its replay, and
reports its own estimate.

# Still open

- **The invader's g is not judged.** Everything downstream of a run reads the invader's
  elasticities at the resident's traits, and they need more nodes than `ln J`: on long
  drought at 108 introductions g is 5.4ε off while `ln J` is 0.3ε off. The next step is to
  judge g on the replay the loop already makes, for about 1.3 forward runs per schedule
  (`refine.md`, Next).
- **Curvatures are not judged,** and the bound's constants were not measured on them.
- **Below scale 1 the estimate can read low** (episodic with a_dG2 ×0.8, above); the spells
  that carry the slow part are not located.
- **The coefficient 0.5 and u come from eight cases;** the bank has ten, plus the held-out
  cases.
- **A bound for short spells** that is not their worst case would return most of the 0.22ε
  set aside.
- **The late spacing caps** (100 and 280 days) are wider than where the square law was
  measured for elasticities.
- invaders' spell ends against the resident's;
- dry-flat's understory, where region replays estimated 1.9× the error;
- which of light or water carries the understory's error.

Settled so far:
- fate's slope jumps only at openings, but spell ends need breakpoints as well;
- with even counts every interval is merged, and the replay costs 0.51–0.66 of a run;
- the last weeks of a spell need a graded density with more intervals, not a breakpoint
  of their own: on dry that took the worst error from 0.79 to 0.36ε (T0, the tuned
  schedule: 0.35) and the estimate to 0.97 of the error;
- the grading's width is t_r, from the traits, not from the drought's length;
- spell ends taken once from the first run serve every level;
- the stop never accepted a run over ε: on five cases started at half scale, every first
  pass was rejected and every second pass accepted;
- the corrected answer Q − e is closer than Q, at no cost;
- at the tolerance 1e-4 a run plus its replay costs 0.92–1.10× the tuned schedule's run
  plus its check, with 38–68% more nodes.
